title: Calm Is More Than One Thing

zones.label: Breathing
zones.summary: Slow breathing can give the body and thinking brain a moment to settle.
facts: Notice the feeling rather than hiding it.
A few comfortable, unforced breaths can slow the rush to react.
Breathing is one option, not a test everyone must do the same way.

zones.label: Movement
zones.summary: Walking, stretching, dance, sport, or other movement can help release tension.
facts: Choose movement that is safe and accessible for your body.
Some people prefer energetic movement; others prefer gentle motion.
Movement traditions can also connect people with culture and community.

zones.label: Art and Music
zones.summary: Drawing, making rhythm, singing, or listening can give feelings a safe form.
facts: Art can express something before words are ready.
Rhythm and music are calming practices in many communities.
The goal is expression and regulation, not artistic perfection.

zones.label: Nature
zones.summary: Outdoor time can create sensory space for reflection and grounding.
facts: Trees, water, gardens, and fresh air can help attention reset.
Connection to land carries deep meaning in many cultures.
Choose a safe place and a practice that fits your family.

zones.label: Connection
zones.summary: Supportive people, shared traditions, prayer, reflection, and community can restore steadiness.
facts: Talking with a trusted person can reduce isolation.
Family and cultural practices are valid sources of coping and belonging.
If distress keeps interfering with daily life, culturally respectful professional help can join the support network.

quiz.question: Which room uses comfortable breaths to make space before reacting?
Which room includes walking, stretching, dance, or sport?
Which room gives feelings form through drawing, rhythm, or listening?
Which room uses safe outdoor sensory space for grounding?
Which room includes trusted people, traditions, prayer, or community support?
